gloss: replacing the lock (of a door); lock replacement

definitions.gloss: replacing the lock (of a door); lock replacement
definitions.explanation: Removing the existing lock — and usually the old key — from a door and installing a new one. Routine when a key is lost, after a break-in, or between residents when a rental property changes hands.

examples.japanese: {鍵|かぎ}{交換|こうかん}を{頼|たの}む。
{鍵|かぎ}を{失|な}くしたので{鍵|かぎ}{交換|こうかん}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: I lost my key, so I need to replace the lock.

examples.japanese: {入居|にゅうきょ}のときに{大家|おおや}さんが{鍵|かぎ}{交換|こうかん}をしてくれた。
examples.english: When I moved in, the landlord replaced the lock for me.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}いシリンダー{錠|じょう}を{防犯|ぼうはん}{性能|せいのう}の{高|たか}いものに{鍵|かぎ}{交換|こうかん}してもらった。
examples.english: I had the old cylinder lock replaced with one with higher security performance.

notes:
Composed of {鍵|かぎ} (key; lock) + {交換|こうかん} (exchange, replacement). In Japanese, {鍵|かぎ} refers both to the key and, loosely, to the lock itself, so {鍵|かぎ}{交換|こうかん} most often means replacing the lock cylinder — not just getting a new key cut.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鍵|かぎ}{交換|こうかん}を{頼|たの}む: to ask to have the lock replaced
- {鍵|かぎ}{交換|こうかん}の{費用|ひよう}: the cost of a lock replacement
- {鍵|かぎ}{交換|こうかん}の{業者|ぎょうしゃ}: a locksmith / lock replacement contractor
- {入居|にゅうきょ}{時|じ}の{鍵|かぎ}{交換|こうかん}: lock replacement at move-in
- {防犯|ぼうはん}{用|よう}の{鍵|かぎ}{交換|こうかん}: lock replacement for security

VERBAL USE:
With する the word acts as a verb: {鍵|かぎ}{交換|こうかん}する — to replace the lock. {してもらう} (to have it done for you) is very common, since most people hire a locksmith rather than doing the work themselves.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {合鍵|あいかぎ}を{作|つく}る: to make a duplicate key — cutting a copy of an existing key, not replacing the lock itself.
- {錠|じょう}{前|まえ}{交換|こうかん}: lock (cylinder) replacement — a more technical synonym; {錠前|じょうまえ} refers unambiguously to the lock mechanism.
- {鍵|かぎ}{修理|しゅうり}: lock repair — fixing a faulty lock rather than replacing it.

USAGE:
In Japanese rental contracts, {鍵|かぎ}{交換|こうかん} is often charged to the new tenant as part of the move-in fees. News stories about break-ins and landlord-tenant disputes also commonly feature the word. Locksmiths advertise heavily under this keyword.
